Subject: DW billing models: seat vs credit vs reserved — recommendations request

Team —

We have the upcoming renewal window and a likely increase in query volume for Q4. I want a concise recommendation on whether we should pursue:

- Committed credits (Snowflake-style)
- On-demand credits (pay-as-you-go)
- Flat-seat / user-based licensing for BI layer (Looker/Metabase)
- Hybrid: credits for compute + seats for BI tools

Please prioritize: cost per 100k queries (rough), operational overhead (SRE + infra), and downgrade risk if we over-commit. Attachments: I pulled the vendor proposals we have so far — see snowflake_commit_quote_aug2026.pdf and gcp_pricing_estimate_aug2026.csv (stubs).

Can you each take an angle: Marcus — cost model + engineer ops impact; Monica — procurement/compliance and SLA implications; Lauren — product/BI seat utilization and forecasting.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: DW billing models: seat vs credit vs reserved — recommendations request

Hannah —

Quick first pass (high level):

- Snowflake committed credits: best unit cost (approx ~30-40% off list) if we can predict sustained concurrency. Upside: lower $/compute. Downside: hard to scale down mid-term, requires a finance commit.

- Snowflake on-demand: flexible, no commit risk, but 1.3–1.6x higher effective cost under steady usage. Good for spiky workloads or pilot projects.

- BigQuery (on-demand & flat-rate): flat-rate slots are closer to committed credits; for sustained analytic workloads flat-rate slots can be cheaper than on-demand but require slot management. GCP submitted a CSV estimate (gcp_pricing_estimate_aug2026.csv).

- BI seats (Looker/Metabase): Metabase seats are inexpensive but lack enterprise governance features; Looker seats cost more but save analyst time via modeled metrics. If we reduce seats we lose self-service velocity.

Operational notes:
- Committed credits reduce cost but increase ops work during initial capacity tuning (slot sizing, caching, query refactors).
- Hybrid model (committed credits for core ETL + on-demand for ad-hoc) gives a good balance.

I'll drop a modeled example in the shared Drive (link below) with a 12/24 month view.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hannah / team —

Attached: procurement_decision_matrix_v2.xlsx (decision matrix + risk scoring). Summary recommendations:

1) Snowflake: pursue a 12-month commit at the mid-tier level (covers baseline ETL traffic + 30% buffer). Rationale: discounts meaningful, preserves the option to top-up for Q4 burst. Require contractual clause: credits rollover for 90 days rolling and clear audit logs for usage.

2) BigQuery: keep as on-demand for ad-hoc ML exploration; consider purchasing flat-rate slots for scheduled heavy batch windows only if our slot saturation reaches >70% for two consecutive weeks.

3) BI layer: negotiate Metabase with an annual seat bundle for core analysts (15 seats) + a small pool of rotatable seats for contractors. Ask Metabase for a usage-based kicker rather than per-seat step-ups.

I flagged procurement-friendly clauses in the matrix (audit, termination for convenience, data export timelines). If legal needs this I can create a redline checklist.

Monica
